text:
sam: Quick run-down from today's thermal/throttle bench for 7B across A100 vs H100 (us-west / us-east / eu-west). Wanted to capture the weirdness we saw with sustained 90% duty cycles. TL;DR: H100 > throughput but observed intermittent thermal-induced p99 blowups on older rack SKUs in us-west; effective $/1M tokens can flip depending on throttling and burst patterns. :chart_with_upwards_trend:

marta: drop the headline numbers pls (p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, $/1M) — and the run command if you have it.

alex: gist of commands we used:
```bash
./bench/run_infer_sweep --model mosaic-7b --quant q8_0 --batch 1 --seq 2048 --mode prefill_decode --gpus a100,h100 --region us-west,us-east,eu-west --duration 20m --measure_latency --emit_metrics json
```
sample output (single-GPU normalized):
```
H100 (older rack): decode tokens/sec: 9200, prefill tokens/sec: 24000, p50/p95/p99 latency(ms): 8 / 35 / 420 (spikes), cost $/1M tokens nominal: $12.8, effective w/ spikes: $16.6
A100 (v4 racks): decode tokens/sec: 6300, prefill tokens/sec: 16000, p50/p95/p99 latency(ms): 12 / 48 / 160, cost $/1M tokens nominal: $10.3
H100 (cooled rack - newer): decode tokens/sec: 9100, p50/p95/p99: 8 / 34 / 95, cost $/1M: $12.6
```

jena: important note — the H100 spike to 420ms aligned with sustained 90% power draw over ~4m windows. We pulled nvml logs and saw power cap events and fan ramping. Older SKUs had slower fan curves so bursts caused transient thermal throttle.

alex: added the nvml snippet we collected:
```text
Timestamp: 2024-11-21T15:32:12Z GPU:0 Power:370W -> 300W (throttle) Temp: 88C Fan: 62% -> 78%
GPU util stayed ~98% while clocks dropped by ~200MHz for ~20s
```

marta: sweet — can you compute how that impacts effective capacity for a 1000 qps service? rough calc pls.

sam: quick ballpark: assume 7B decoding at 0.5 tokens per request avg (small prompts) -> tokens/sec per GPU is primary metric. Under no-throttle H100 9200 t/s -> 9200 * 3600 = 33.12M tokens/hr -> nominal $/1M = $12.8 so $424/hr per GPU equivalent. Under throttling (20% time at reduced clocks ~ effective t/s drops to 7400) the hour average tokens/hr -> ~29.16M -> effective $/1M becomes $14.4. For capacity: to sustain 1000 qps * 0.5 tok = 500 t/s -> a single H100 nominally supports ~9200/500 = 18.4x headroom (but with throttles drops to ~14.8x). A100 would be ~6300/500 = 12.6x. So you still need fewer GPUs with H100 but the headroom margin shrinks when throttling.

jena: also saw quantization interactions — q4_0 had slightly fewer thermal events because lower power draw, tokens/sec delta ~ -6% vs q8_0 but much smoother p99. Worth considering for steady-state customer workloads.

alex: plotted region breakdown quickly (very rough):
- us-west (older racks): H100 effective $/1M = $16.6, A100 = $10.3
- us-east (cooled racks): H100 effective $/1M = $12.6, A100 = $10.1
- eu-west (mixed): H100 ~13.8, A100 ~10.5

marta: so decision matrix for provisioning: if you need raw peak throughput (bursty short-lived) H100 still wins; if you need predictable p99 and lowest $/1M for sustained 24/7 throughput, A100 or H100 in cooled racks with quantization might be better.

sam: proposed actions:
1) Flag older us-west racks for fan/thermal audit with infra.
2) Add automatic SKU-mapped thermal profiles to scheduler so we prefer cooler racks for H100-heavy offers.
3) Add q4_0 baseline run for customer-facing steady-state pricing page (we can publish $/1M under typical configs).
4) Re-run 24h soak on a13 (newer H100) and post updated p99 distribution.
